info.title: Angel clinic engine
info.description:
The server behind the app: senses each day against the person's own normal, holds attention when something changes, responds with one small action, and learns which action helped. It never diagnoses.

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Device tokens come from `POST /v1/devices/pair`; clinician session tokens from `POST /v1/clinic/login`; admin tokens from the seed script.

Errors always look like `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}`.

post.summary: Exchange a one-time pairing code for a device token
post.description:
No auth. The code is one-time and expires. The returned token is shown
once: keep it in the Keychain.

post.summary: Upload one day or a batch of history
post.description:
Upsert by date. Values that cannot be true (negative, absurd, future
dates, conflicting duplicates in one batch) are rejected per day, logged,
and never used for the baseline.

post.summary: Upload an Apple Health summary: any HealthKit type, one value per day
post.description:
For the HealthKit harness app and a watch companion. Post the harness's
`HealthDataSummary` JSON as it is: only `metrics[].typeIdentifier`, `unit`,
`aggregation` and `daily[].day`, `count`, `sum`, `mean` are read; everything
else is ignored and never stored (source and device names, single samples).

Every type is stored per day (upsert by type and day; the most recent 400
days are kept). Steps, walking speed (m/s), sleep (hours) and HRV (SDNN, ms)
also fill the day records, with the same checks as `POST /v1/daily`, so the
comparison with the person's own normal sees them. Send it as often as you
like; unchanged days are not written again. The body may be up to 4 MiB:
send about 90 days per call, or the types in several calls.

post.summary: Send one activity record: focus, breathing or check-in
post.description:
One record per activity, idempotent by `id`: the same record again is
answered without new XP; a different record under a used id is refused
(409). Values that cannot be true are rejected (422) and logged.

Typed words in a check-in are untrusted data with exactly the note's
treatment: classified into enums only, never followed, never logged,
never sent outside the server. If they ask for help, `crisis` is true and
the help block is included, as for a note.

The answer says what Lanvi shows next: XP gained, the new total, stage,
glow and one line from the fixed set. XP is for showing up: the same
whatever the score.

Sensors: `sensors` (docs/sensors.md) carries the Apple Watch's heart-rate and
HRV samples during the activity and every game moment, with one clock anchor
that lines them up with `face_raw`. The server computes the summary and keeps
the rows.

The face: send `face_raw` (raw ARKit frames, numbers only; the server
computes every face measure, docs/face-raw.md) or, from older clients,
`face` (a summary the phone computed). Not both (422). This route accepts
bodies up to MAX_FACE_RAW_BODY_BYTES (4 MiB by default); other routes keep
the general limit.

get.summary: Status, today's suggestion, Lanvi and the crisis block
get.description:
`crisis` is always present. `status` is one of no_baseline, within,
outside, no_data; missing data is shown as no_data, never as within.
`lanvi` holds XP, stage, glow, the wandering (with a story when one waits)
and the line Lanvi says today. `round_config` is deprecated.

post.summary: Answer a suggestion
post.description: Idempotent by `id`. Answers are enums only.

404.description: Not found (or not in your tenant)

post.summary: A few words from the patient (the only free-text field)
post.description:
The text is untrusted data. It is classified into enums (code lexicon
plus the local model through the gates), never followed as an
instruction and never logged. When `crisis` is true the help block is
included and the reply is the fixed help line.

CHAT_MODE=fixed (default): the reply is a fixed template and the text is
never sent outside the server.
CHAT_MODE=gemini: for a note that did not open the help screen, and only
for a patient who allowed outside processing, the note and today's earlier
turns go to Gemini, which writes Lanvi's reply (`template_id: gemini`),
checked by code. Any failure gives the fixed template.

get.description:

and HRV rows with HealthKit's own times (ms from started_at), every game moment on

get.summary: Raw model exchanges: what was sent to a model and what it answered
get.description:
Newest first. Each item holds the messages sent, the raw reply (null when the
model did not answer), the model name, the time it took and the trace chain it
belongs to. What code did with the reply is in the trace. A note's prompt
contains the patient's words; that message is hidden unless the patient shares
their notes.

get.summary: How the mind reasoned: chains of steps per trigger, newest first
get.description:
Each chain ties together everything one trigger caused, layer by layer:
trigger, watchers, attention, response (code), level 1, level 2, notifier,
learning. `current` explains each held attention item: its level, the rule
that set it, and what the system last did about it. Codes, ids, enums and
numbers only: never note text.

post.description:
Range-checked against the hypotheses file. One rating per day and scale:
recording the same day and scale again replaces it. Used only as the
reference of the association appraisal.

get.summary: The latest association appraisal: how the measures moved with the reference
get.description:
A within-person description of how this person's measurements moved
together over time. Not validated, not a diagnosis; never shown to the
patient. Statistics by code; a level-1 model may add caveats and the
overall judgement, and code corrects whatever it got wrong (per field,
`*_source` and `sources` say so). `status: none` until it has run.

post.summary: Run the level-2 reading again for one activity (or an earlier round)
post.description:
With `activity_id`: the session reading of a focus or breathing session
with a face summary, or with `what: "frames"` the frame reading of a session
sent with raw face frames (level 2 reads them, code checks every item;
returns the stored `frames_reading`). With `round_id`: the movement reading
of an AR round of the earlier design.

post.summary: Compute the face summary of a patient's raw sessions again
post.description:
For every focus or breathing session sent with raw face frames: compute
the summary again from the stored frames with the current thresholds, and
rewrite its face summary, face quality and face z values. Sessions sent with
a summary are left as they are. Returns how many were recomputed.

xp_gained.title: Xp Gained
xp_gained.description: XP this record earned now (0 when re-sent).

glow.title: Glow
glow.description: 0 to 1. A full glow starts a wandering.

line.description: One line for Lanvi to say now, from a fixed set.

crisis.title: Crisis
crisis.description: True when typed check-in words asked for help.

reading.title: Reading
reading.description: The session reading (level 2) for a focus or breathing session with a face summary: pending, or off / not_allowed. not_applicable for a check-in or a session without a face summary. Fetch the line from GET /v1/activities/{id}/reading.

line.title: Line
line.description: Neutral line for the patient, from a fixed set. Never about mood or the face.

line.title: Line
line.description: Plain line for the patient, from a fixed set.

what.title: What
what.description: With activity_id: `session` runs the session reading, `frames` the frame reading (level 2 reads the raw face frames, code checks every item; the activity must have been sent with face_raw). `days`, without an id: the day reading (level 2 reads the daily numbers of the last weeks, code checks every item).

text.title: Text
text.description: Plain text for the code, from a fixed set.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model's value when it was a known code; null otherwise.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: What one observation is: a rating (the measure is averaged over the week up to it) or a day (proxy reference).

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Per field: model, code, or code_corrected.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.description: Ratings of that scale, when a rating.

expected.title: Expected
expected.description: Direction the research literature leads us to expect when symptoms are worse.

status.title: Status
status.description: insufficient: fewer paired days than design.min_n, no statistics. is_reference: this measure is the proxy reference itself.

n.title: N
n.description: Paired observations: ratings (design.unit rating) or days.

rho.title: Rho
rho.description: Spearman rho, oriented: positive = moves in the expected direction when symptoms are worse. For 'mixed' positive = higher when the reference is worse.

lead_days.title: Lead Days
lead_days.description: Lag -3..3 with the largest oriented association; negative = the measure moves first.

contrast.title: Contrast
contrast.description: Cliff's delta, days with attention held against other days, oriented like rho.

agreement_source.title: Agreement Source
agreement_source.description: model, code (no model), or code_corrected (the model's value was replaced).

series.title: Series
series.description: Day-by-day values behind the statistics, for charts: first_day, last_day, reference [[day, value]] and measures {key: [[day, value]]}; day counts from first_day.

id.title: Id
id.description: Client-generated id. Re-sending the same record is safe and earns nothing twice; a different record under the same id is refused (409).

suggestion_id.title: Suggestion Id
suggestion_id.description: The suggestion this answers, if it was played from one.

sensors.description: The Apple Watch's heart data and the game moments during the activity (docs/sensors.md).

face.description: A summary the phone computed. Prefer face_raw: the server computes the summary.

face_raw.description: Raw ARKit frames; the server computes the face summary. Not with face.

id.description: Client-generated id. Re-sending the same record is safe and earns nothing twice; a different record under the same id is refused (409).

suggestion_id.title: Suggestion Id
suggestion_id.description: The suggestion this answers, if it was played from one.

sensors.description: The Apple Watch's heart data and the game moments during the activity (docs/sensors.md).

good_things.title: Good Things
good_things.description: Up to 3 good things from today.

plan.description: One small nice thing for tomorrow.

plan_done.title: Plan Done
plan_done.description: Whether yesterday's plan happened, when the app asked.

CheckinItem.title: CheckinItem
CheckinItem.description:
Either a catalog id the person tapped, or a few typed words (not both).
Typed text is untrusted data: classified like a note, never followed,
never logged, never sent outside the server.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Demo panel allowed for this clinician.

reviewed_by_clinician.title: Reviewed By Clinician
reviewed_by_clinician.description: False while the wording is a draft; show it as draft wording.

days.title: Days
days.description: One day, or a batch of history. Upsert by date.

rate_hz.title: Rate Hz
rate_hz.description: Frames per second of `samples`. 30 is enough.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Names in the order of each sample's values: ARKit blend-shape identifiers (e.g. mouthSmileLeft) and headPitch, headYaw, headRoll (degrees, headPitch positive = chin down). Must include mouthSmileLeft, mouthSmileRight, eyeBlinkLeft, eyeBlinkRight.

samples.title: Samples
samples.description: One row per frame, len(channels) values each.

tracked.title: Tracked
tracked.description: Optional, one per frame: 1 when ARKit tracked the face. Default all 1.

moments_ms.title: Moments Ms
moments_ms.description: Optional: times of marked pleasant moments, ms from the first frame.

FaceRawIn.title: FaceRawIn
FaceRawIn.description:
Raw ARKit frames from the front camera during the activity, when the
person allowed it. The phone computes nothing: the server derives the face
summary (docs/face-raw.md). Numbers only: blend-shape coefficients 0 to 1
and head angles in degrees. No image, no video, no mesh, no identifiers.

tracked.title: Tracked
tracked.description: As sent; null means all frames tracked.

FaceRawOut.title: FaceRawOut
FaceRawOut.description:
The stored raw frames of one activity, as the phone sent them, for
research download. Numbers only.

facial_activity.title: Facial Activity
facial_activity.description: How much the face moved, 0 to 1.

look_down_share.title: Look Down Share
look_down_share.description: Share of time looking down, 0 to 1.

smile_time_share.title: Smile Time Share
smile_time_share.description: Share of the time smiling, 0 to 1.

eye_smile_share.title: Eye Smile Share
eye_smile_share.description: Share of smiles with a cheek raise (reaching the eyes), 0 to 1.

smile_response_share.title: Smile Response Share
smile_response_share.description: Share of marked pleasant moments in the activity followed by a smile shortly after, 0 to 1.

smile_response_latency_s.title: Smile Response Latency S
smile_response_latency_s.description: Median delay from a marked pleasant moment to the smile, seconds.

brow_down_share.title: Brow Down Share
brow_down_share.description: Share of the time with brows drawn down, 0 to 1.

inner_brow_up_share.title: Inner Brow Up Share
inner_brow_up_share.description: Share of the time with inner brows raised, 0 to 1.

head_pitch_deg.title: Head Pitch Deg
head_pitch_deg.description: Average head angle, degrees; looking down is higher.

head_movement.title: Head Movement
head_movement.description: How much the head moved, 0 to 1.

tracking_quality.title: Tracking Quality
tracking_quality.description: 0 to 1. Below 0.6 the summary is kept but never used for the person's own normal.

FaceSummary.title: FaceSummary
FaceSummary.description:
Numbers only, from the front camera during the activity, when the person
allowed it. No frames, no images, no landmarks.

suggestion_id.title: Suggestion Id

reaction_ms.description: Reaction time per tap in whole milliseconds. The server computes its own statistics.

face.description: A summary the phone computed. Prefer face_raw: the server computes the summary.

day.title: Day
day.description: Calendar day, yyyy-MM-dd, in the phone's time zone.

mean.title: Mean
mean.description: The day's value: the sum for summed types, the mean for averaged ones, hours for sleep.

typeIdentifier.title: Typeidentifier
typeIdentifier.description: The HealthKit identifier, for example HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRestingHeartRate.

days.title: Days
days.description: Days of this type now stored.

days_updated.title: Days Updated
days_updated.description: Days whose steps, walking speed, sleep or HRV changed from this upload.

line.description: The line Lanvi says today, from the fixed set.

plan_to_ask.description: Yesterday's plan, to ask about in tonight's check-in; null if none.

text.title: Text
text.description: The ONLY free-text field in the API. Untrusted data: classified, never followed. Never sent outside the server, except with CHAT_MODE=gemini (default fixed), where a note that did not open the help screen goes to Gemini so it can write Lanvi's reply.

template_id.title: Template Id
template_id.description: A fixed line's id, or `gemini` when Gemini wrote the reply (CHAT_MODE=gemini).

pairing_code.title: Pairing Code
pairing_code.description: One-time code from the clinic, e.g. ABCD-EFGH-JKLM.

device_label.title: Device Label
device_label.description: Short label for the device. Not a person's name.

device_token.title: Device Token
device_token.description: Bearer token. Shown once; store it in the Keychain.

plan_id.title: Plan Id
plan_id.description: Catalog id, or null when the plan was typed (the app has the words on the phone).

helps.title: Helps
helps.description: What helps, in the order the person chose. The starting order of suggestions.

date.title: Date
date.description: The day the rating describes (clinic local).

score.title: Score
score.description: Total score. Range per scale: phq9 0 to 27, phq2 0 to 6, clinician_global 1 to 7.

recomputed.title: Recomputed
recomputed.description: Raw sessions whose face summary was computed again.

id.title: Id
id.description: Client-generated id. Re-sending the same id is an upsert.

after_round.title: After Round
after_round.description: {template_id, text}: one line to show after the round.

started_uptime_s.title: Started Uptime S
started_uptime_s.description: The phone's monotonic clock (CACurrentMediaTime, the clock of ARFrame.timestamp) at started_at. With started_at this anchors every time below.

SensorMomentIn.title: SensorMomentIn
SensorMomentIn.description:
One game moment (GameMoments.swift): the name, its time on both clocks, and the
small number it carried (reaction ms, breath number, finished 1 or 0) or the
check-in step. Never typed words or picked labels.

workout.title: Workout
workout.description: Recorded inside an HKWorkoutSession with a live builder.

started_ms.title: Started Ms
started_ms.description: When the watch began recording, ms from started_at.

heart_rate.title: Heart Rate
heart_rate.description: [t_ms, bpm] rows, oldest first, wall clock.

hrv_sdnn.title: Hrv Sdnn
hrv_sdnn.description: [t_ms, sdnn_ms] rows, whenever the watch wrote one.

face_offset_ms.title: Face Offset Ms
face_offset_ms.description: The first face_raw frame, ms from started_at on the monotonic clock. Frame i is then at face_offset_ms + i * 1000 / rate_hz.

SensorsIn.title: SensorsIn
SensorsIn.description:
What the Apple Watch and the game said during the activity (docs/sensors.md).
Times are milliseconds from started_at. Heart-rate and HRV rows keep HealthKit's
own sample times; the server computes every summary and keeps the rows.

round_config.title: Round Config
round_config.description: Deprecated: for apps of the earlier AR design only.

headline.title: Headline
headline.description: At most 6 words, from a fixed set, for one row.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: The most important thing the chain did.

level_rule.title: Level Rule
level_rule.description: The rule that set the current level.

layer.title: Layer
layer.description: Step of the loop, in this order: trigger, watchers, attention, response, level1, level2, notifier, learning.

code.title: Code
code.description: Short machine code for what happened, e.g. opened, suggested.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Codes, ids, enums and numbers only. Never note text.

notable.title: Notable
notable.description: This step changed something: opened or raised attention, made a suggestion, sent or queued a message, or refused a model answer.

state.title: State
state.description: home: nothing going on; away: Lanvi is wandering until returns_at; back: a story waits for an answer.

bearer.description: Opaque bearer token (device, clinician session, or admin).
